metadata.title: Simple Statistical Gradient-Following Algorithms for Connectionist Reinforcement Learning
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Stochastic semilinear unit
nodes.statement: A unit whose output $y_i$ is drawn from a distribution with single parameter $p_i = f(s_i)$, where $f$ is a differentiable squashing function and $s_i = w_i^T x_i = \sum_j w_{ij} x_j$.
nodes.statement_clean: A stochastic unit that draws its output from a distribution whose single parameter is the squashed weighted sum of inputs.

nodes.name: Bernoulli semilinear unit
nodes.statement: A stochastic semilinear unit whose output $y_i$ is a Bernoulli random variable with parameter $p_i$, so $\Pr\{y_i=1 \mid w_i, x_i\} = p_i$ and $\Pr\{y_i=0 \mid w_i, x_i\} = 1 - p_i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Stochastic semilinear unit whose output is 0 or 1 with probability controlled by the squashed weighted sum.

nodes.name: Bernoulli-logistic unit
nodes.statement: A Bernoulli semilinear unit with logistic squashing function $f(s_i) = 1/(1 + e^{-s_i})$.
nodes.statement_clean: A Bernoulli semilinear unit whose squashing function is the logistic.

nodes.name: Gaussian unit
nodes.statement: A stochastic unit whose output $y$ is drawn from a normal distribution with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$, where $\mu, \sigma$ are computed deterministically from the unit's weights and input.
nodes.statement_clean: Stochastic unit whose output is normally distributed with deterministically computed mean and standard deviation.

nodes.name: Characteristic eligibility
nodes.statement: For a parameter $w_{ij}$, the quantity $e_{ij} = \partial \ln g_i / \partial w_{ij}$, where $g_i(\xi, w_i, x_i) = \Pr\{y_i = \xi \mid w_i, x_i\}$ is the unit's probability mass/density function.
nodes.statement_clean: The partial derivative of the log-likelihood of the unit's output with respect to a weight.

nodes.name: Expected reinforcement performance criterion
nodes.statement: The performance measure $E\{r \mid W\}$, the expected value of the reinforcement signal $r$ conditioned on the network's weight matrix $W$, assumed well-defined under stationarity and independence of inputs.
nodes.statement_clean: Performance measure to optimize: expected reinforcement given the network weights.

nodes.name: REINFORCE algorithm (class)
nodes.statement: Any learning algorithm in which $\Delta w_{ij} = \alpha_{ij}(r - b_{ij}) e_{ij}$, where $\alpha_{ij} \ge 0$ is a learning rate, $b_{ij}$ a reinforcement baseline (independent of $y_i$ given $W, x_i$), and $e_{ij} = \partial \ln g_i / \partial w_{ij}$.
nodes.statement_clean: A class of weight-update rules of form REward Increment = Nonnegative Factor x Offset Reinforcement x Characteristic Eligibility.

nodes.name: Reinforcement baseline
nodes.statement: A quantity $b_{ij}$ subtracted from the reinforcement $r$ in a REINFORCE update, conditionally independent of $y_i$ given $W$ and $x_i$.
nodes.statement_clean: Subtracted reference value in REINFORCE updates that does not bias the gradient estimate.

nodes.name: Reinforcement comparison
nodes.statement: A baseline strategy that maintains an adaptive estimate $\bar{r}$ of upcoming reinforcement, e.g. $\bar{r}(t) = \gamma r(t-1) + (1-\gamma) \bar{r}(t-1)$ with $0 < \gamma \le 1$, used as $b_{ij}$ in the REINFORCE update.
nodes.statement_clean: Use of an exponentially averaged past reinforcement as the baseline in REINFORCE updates.

nodes.name: Episodic learning task
nodes.statement: A learning setup where a network $N$ is trained on episodes of $k$ time steps each, with a single reinforcement value $r$ delivered at the end of each episode.
nodes.statement_clean: Training scenario in which one reinforcement value is given per fixed-length episode.

nodes.name: Unfolding-in-time mapping
nodes.statement: A construction associating to a recurrent network $N$ run over a fixed period an acyclic network $N^*$ obtained by duplicating $N$ once per time step, with each weight $w_{ij}$ replicated as $\{w^t_{ij}\}$ all equal across time.
nodes.statement_clean: Standard time-unrolling that turns a recurrent network into an equivalent feedforward network for analysis.

nodes.name: Episodic REINFORCE algorithm
nodes.statement: A learning rule of the form $\Delta w_{ij} = \alpha_{ij}(r - b_{ij}) \sum_{t=1}^{k} e_{ij}(t)$ applied at the end of each $k$-step episode, with $e_{ij}(t)$ the characteristic eligibility at time $t$ and standard REINFORCE conditions on $\alpha_{ij}, b_{ij}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Episode-level extension of REINFORCE that accumulates per-step characteristic eligibilities before updating.

nodes.name: Model-based reinforcement learning algorithm
nodes.statement: An algorithm that explicitly estimates relevant parameters of the system to be controlled (or of the reinforcement function) and uses the learned model to compute parameter adjustments; for gradient methods, the model must yield estimates of the gradient of expected reinforcement.
nodes.statement_clean: Reinforcement learner that builds an explicit model of the reinforcement function and uses it to compute updates.
nodes.origin_citation: Barto, Sutton & Watkins 1990; cf. Goodwin & Sin 1984

nodes.name: Characteristic eligibility for Bernoulli parameter
nodes.statement: $\partial \ln g_i / \partial p_i = (y_i - p_i) / [p_i(1 - p_i)]$ (equation (5)), valid for $p_i \notin \{0,1\}$.

nodes.name: Characteristic eligibility for Bernoulli semilinear weight
nodes.statement: $\partial \ln g_i / \partial w_{ij} = \frac{y_i - p_i}{p_i(1 - p_i)} f'(s_i) x_j$ (equation (6)).

nodes.name: Characteristic eligibility for Bernoulli-logistic weight
nodes.statement: $\partial \ln g_i / \partial w_{ij} = (y_i - p_i) x_j$ (equation (7)), since $f'(s_i) = p_i(1 - p_i)$ for the logistic.

nodes.name: REINFORCE update for Bernoulli-logistic network
nodes.statement: $\Delta w_{ij} = \alpha r (y_i - p_i) x_j$ (equation (8)), obtained by setting $\alpha_{ij} = \alpha$ and $b_{ij} = 0$.

nodes.name: REINFORCE with reinforcement comparison (Bernoulli-logistic)
nodes.statement: $\Delta w_{ij} = \alpha (r - \bar{r})(y_i - p_i) x_j$ (equation (9)), with $\bar{r}$ updated by exponential averaging $\bar{r}(t) = \gamma r(t-1) + (1-\gamma) \bar{r}(t-1)$.

nodes.name: Characteristic eligibility for Gaussian mean
nodes.statement: $\partial \ln g / \partial \mu = (y - \mu) / \sigma^2$ (equation (12)).

nodes.name: Characteristic eligibility for Gaussian standard deviation
nodes.statement: $\partial \ln g / \partial \sigma = [(y - \mu)^2 - \sigma^2] / \sigma^3$.

nodes.name: REINFORCE update for Gaussian mean
nodes.statement: $\Delta \mu = \alpha_\mu (r - b_\mu) (y - \mu)/\sigma^2$ (equation (13)).

nodes.name: REINFORCE update for Gaussian standard deviation
nodes.statement: $\Delta \sigma = \alpha_\sigma (r - b_\sigma)[(y - \mu)^2 - \sigma^2]/\sigma^3$ (equation (14)).

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (REINFORCE gradient property)
nodes.statement:
For any REINFORCE algorithm, $\langle E\{\Delta W \mid W\}, 
abla_W E\{r \mid W\}angle \ge 0$. If $\alpha_{ij} > 0$ for all $i,j$, equality holds iff $
abla_W E\{r \mid W\} = 0$. If $\alpha_{ij} = \alpha$ is constant, $E\{\Delta W \mid W\} = \alpha 
abla_W E\{r \mid W\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: REINFORCE updates have nonnegative inner product with the true gradient of expected reinforcement, and are an unbiased gradient estimator when the rate is uniform.
assumptions: Algorithm has form $\Delta w_{ij} = \alpha_{ij}(r - b_{ij}) e_{ij}$ with $b_{ij}$ conditionally independent of $y_i$ given $W, x_i$
conclusions: $E\{\Delta W \mid W\} = \alpha \nabla_W E\{r \mid W\}$ when $\alpha_{ij} = \alpha$ constant

nodes.name: Theorem 2 (Episodic REINFORCE gradient property)
nodes.statement:
For any episodic REINFORCE algorithm, $\langle E\{\Delta W \mid W\}, 
abla_W E\{r \mid W\}angle \ge 0$. If $\alpha_{ij} > 0$, equality holds iff $
abla_W E\{r \mid W\} = 0$. If $\alpha_{ij} = \alpha$ constant, $E\{\Delta W \mid W\} = \alpha 
abla_W E\{r \mid W\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Episodic REINFORCE has the same gradient-following property as the immediate-reinforcement version.
assumptions: Algorithm has form $\Delta w_{ij} = \alpha_{ij}(r - b_{ij}) \sum_{t=1}^{k} e_{ij}(t)$
$\alpha_{ij}$ depends at most on $w_i$ and episode number
conclusions: $E\{\Delta W \mid W\} = \alpha \nabla_W E\{r \mid W\}$ when $\alpha_{ij} = \alpha$ constant

nodes.name: Proposition 1 (Characteristic eligibility of mean for exponential families)
nodes.statement: If $g(y, \mu, \theta_2, \ldots, \theta_k) = \exp[Q(\mu,\theta_2,\ldots,\theta_k) y + D(\mu,\theta_2,\ldots,\theta_k) + S(y)]$ where $\mu$ is the mean, then $\partial \ln g / \partial \mu = (y - \mu)/\sigma^2$, with $\sigma^2$ the variance.
nodes.statement_clean: For exponential-family distributions parameterized so that the natural mean is mu, the log-likelihood derivative w.r.t. mu equals (y-mu)/sigma^2.
assumptions: $g$ is a probability mass or density function of the stated exponential form
$\mu$ is the mean of the distribution

nodes.name: Fact 1 (Conditional expected reinforcement derivative)
nodes.statement: $\partial E\{r \mid W, x_i\} / \partial w_{ij} = \sum_{\xi \in Y_i} E\{r \mid W, x_i, y_i = \xi\} \, \partial g_i(\xi, w_i, x_i)/\partial w_{ij}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The partial derivative of conditional expected reinforcement decomposes as a sum over outputs of conditional expectations weighted by derivatives of $g_i$.
conclusions: $\partial E\{r \mid W, x_i\} / \partial w_{ij} = \sum_\xi E\{r \mid W, x_i, y_i = \xi\} \partial g_i / \partial w_{ij}$

nodes.name: Fact 2 (Sum of derivatives of probabilities is zero)
nodes.statement: $\sum_{\xi \in Y_i} \partial g_i(\xi, w_i, x_i) / \partial w_{ij} = 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Differentiating the normalization $\sum_\xi g_i = 1$ gives a zero sum of derivatives.
assumptions: $g_i$ is a probability mass function summing to 1

nodes.name: Lemma 1 (Conditional expected REINFORCE update)
nodes.statement: For any REINFORCE algorithm, $E\{\Delta w_{ij} \mid W, x_i\} = \alpha_{ij} \, \partial E\{r \mid W, x_i\}/\partial w_{ij}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Conditional on input to the unit, the expected REINFORCE update equals the rate factor times the conditional gradient.
conclusions: $E\{\Delta w_{ij} \mid W, x_i\} = \alpha_{ij} \, \partial E\{r \mid W, x_i\}/\partial w_{ij}$

nodes.name: Fact 3 (Marginal gradient via conditional)
nodes.statement: $\partial E\{r \mid W\} / \partial w_{ij} = \sum_{x \in X_i} \partial E\{r \mid W, x_i = x\}/\partial w_{ij} \cdot \Pr\{x_i = x \mid W\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Marginal gradient of expected reinforcement w.r.t. $w_{ij}$ is the input-averaged conditional gradient.
assumptions: $\Pr\{x_i = x \mid W\}$ does not depend on $w_{ij}$ (weight $w_{ij}$ is downstream of $x_i$)
conclusions: $\partial E\{r \mid W\}/\partial w_{ij} = \sum_x \partial E\{r \mid W, x_i = x\}/\partial w_{ij} \cdot \Pr\{x_i = x \mid W\}$

nodes.name: Lemma 2 (Marginal expected REINFORCE update)
nodes.statement: For any REINFORCE algorithm, $E\{\Delta w_{ij} \mid W\} = \alpha_{ij} \, \partial E\{r \mid W\}/\partial w_{ij}$.
nodes.statement_clean: The marginal expected REINFORCE update equals the rate times the gradient of expected reinforcement.
assumptions: $\alpha_{ij}$ does not depend on input to unit

nodes.name: Fact 4 (Episodic gradient via unfolding)
nodes.statement: $\partial E\{r \mid W\} / \partial w_{ij} = \sum_{t=1}^{k} \partial E\{r \mid W^*\} / \partial w^t_{ij}$, where $w^t_{ij}$ are the time-replicated weights in the unfolded network $N^*$.
nodes.statement_clean: Gradient w.r.t. a recurrent weight equals the sum of gradients w.r.t. its time-unfolded copies.
assumptions: $w^t_{ij} = w_{ij}$ for all $t$ (weights tied across time in unfolding)
conclusions: $\partial E\{r \mid W\}/\partial w_{ij} = \sum_{t=1}^{k} \partial E\{r \mid W^*\}/\partial w^t_{ij}$

nodes.name: Lemma 3 (Expected episodic REINFORCE update)
nodes.statement: For any episodic REINFORCE algorithm, $E\{\Delta w_{ij} \mid W\} = \alpha_{ij} \, \partial E\{r \mid W\}/\partial w_{ij}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Marginal expected episodic REINFORCE update is rate times the gradient of expected reinforcement.
assumptions: Per-step updates $\Delta w^t_{ij}$ form REINFORCE algorithm in unfolded $N^*$

nodes.name: REINFORCE algorithm
nodes.statement: Per-trial weight update $\Delta w_{ij} = \alpha_{ij}(r - b_{ij}) e_{ij}$ for each parameter, climbing the gradient of expected reinforcement without explicit gradient computation.
input: Reinforcement signal $r$ at end of trial
Per-parameter baseline $b_{ij}$ conditionally independent of $y_i$ given $W, x_i$
output: Updated weight matrix $W$ via $w_{ij} \gets w_{ij} + \alpha_{ij}(r - b_{ij}) e_{ij}$

nodes.name: REINFORCE with reinforcement comparison
nodes.statement: REINFORCE update $\Delta w_{ij} = \alpha (r - \bar{r})(y_i - p_i) x_j$ for Bernoulli-logistic units, with adaptive baseline $\bar{r}(t) = \gamma r(t-1) + (1-\gamma) \bar{r}(t-1)$.

nodes.name: Episodic REINFORCE algorithm
nodes.statement: At episode end, update $\Delta w_{ij} = \alpha_{ij}(r - b_{ij}) \sum_{t=1}^{k} e_{ij}(t)$, accumulating per-step characteristic eligibilities and applying the offset reinforcement once.
input: Per-step characteristic eligibilities $e_{ij}(t)$ accumulated during the episode

nodes.name: REINFORCE for Gaussian unit
nodes.statement: Update Gaussian-unit parameters by $\Delta \mu = \alpha_\mu (r - b_\mu)(y - \mu)/\sigma^2$ and $\Delta \sigma = \alpha_\sigma (r - b_\sigma)[(y - \mu)^2 - \sigma^2]/\sigma^3$.

nodes.name: Backpropagation through deterministic hidden units (REINFORCE-BP)
nodes.statement: For a network with stochastic outputs and deterministic hidden units, compute each weight's characteristic eligibility $\partial \ln g / \partial w_{ij} = \sum_{k \in O} \partial \ln g_k / \partial w_{ij}$ by injecting per-output-unit eligibility signals and running standard backpropagation.
input: Network with deterministic hidden units, stochastic output units (index set $O$)
Per-output-unit characteristic eligibility, e.g. $\partial \ln g_k / \partial p_k = (y_k - p_k)/[p_k(1-p_k)]$
output: Unbiased gradient estimates $\partial E\{r \mid W\}/\partial w_{ij}$ via backward pass
Weight updates $\Delta w_{ij} = \alpha_{ij}(r - b_{ij}) \partial \ln g/\partial w_{ij}$

nodes.name: Backpropagation through Gaussian random number generator
nodes.statement: Treat output as $y = \mu + \sigma z$ with $z$ a standard normal, then propagate $\partial J/\partial y$ through to $\partial J/\partial \mu = \partial J/\partial y$ and $\partial J/\partial \sigma = \partial J/\partial y \cdot (y - \mu)/\sigma$.
output: Partial derivatives $\partial J/\partial \mu$ and $\partial J/\partial \sigma$ via reparameterization

nodes.name: REINFORCE variant with output-mean eligibility ($y - \bar{y}$)
nodes.statement: For a single Bernoulli-logistic unit with bias weight $w$, update $\Delta w = \alpha(r - \bar{r})(y - \bar{y})$ where $\bar{y}(t) = \gamma y(t-1) + (1-\gamma)\bar{y}(t-1)$ replaces $p$ with an exponentially averaged $\bar{y}$.

nodes.name: Linear reward-inaction (LR-I) stochastic learning automaton
nodes.statement: Two-action stochastic learning automaton update $\Delta p_i = \alpha_i r (y_i - p_i)$ when reinforcement is in $\{0,1\}$; the special-case REINFORCE algorithm for a single Bernoulli unit with $b_i = 0$ and $\alpha_i = \alpha p_i(1 - p_i)$.

nodes.name: Associative reward-penalty (AR-P) algorithm
nodes.statement: $\Delta w_{ij} = \alpha[r(y_i - p_i) + \lambda(1 - r)(1 - y_i - p_i)] x_j$ for $r \in [0,1]$ and $0 < \lambda \le 1$; reduces to the AR-I algorithm (a Bernoulli-logistic REINFORCE) when $\lambda = 0$.
nodes.origin_citation: Barto 1985; Barto & Anandan 1985; Barto & Anderson 1985; Barto & Jordan 1987

nodes.name: Backpropagation (chain-rule backward pass)
nodes.statement: Gradient computation in feedforward networks of deterministic units by recursively applying the chain rule in a backward pass to obtain partial derivatives of an output functional with respect to all weights.
nodes.origin_citation: leCun 1985; Parker 1985; Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams 1986; Werbos 1974

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: Combine Lemma 2 with the inner-product expansion to get $\langle E\{\Delta W \mid W\}, \nabla_W E\{r\mid W\}\rangle = \sum_{i,j} \alpha_{ij} (\partial E\{r \mid W\}/\partial w_{ij})^2 \ge 0$, with equality conditions immediate.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Identical structure to Theorem 1's proof: by Lemma 3, $\langle E\{\Delta W \mid W\}, \nabla_W E\{r\mid W\}\rangle = \sum_{i,j} \alpha_{ij}(\partial E\{r \mid W\}/\partial w_{ij})^2 \ge 0$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 1
nodes.statement: Differentiating $\sum_y g = 1$ and $\sum_y y g = \mu$ w.r.t. $\mu$ yields constraints $\alpha \mu + \beta = 0$ and $\alpha \sigma^2 = 1$ where $\partial \ln g/\partial \mu = \alpha y + \beta$; solving gives $\alpha = 1/\sigma^2, \beta = -\mu/\sigma^2$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2 to expand inner product
nodes.statement: Write $\langle E\{\Delta W \mid W\}, \nabla_W E\{r \mid W\}\rangle = \sum_{(i,j)\in I} E\{\Delta w_{ij} \mid W\} \partial E\{r \mid W\}/\partial w_{ij}$ and substitute $E\{\Delta w_{ij} \mid W\} = \alpha_{ij} \partial E\{r\mid W\}/\partial w_{ij}$ from Lemma 2.

nodes.name: Conclude as sum of nonnegative squares
nodes.statement: The expression becomes $\sum_{(i,j)\in I} \alpha_{ij} (\partial E\{r \mid W\}/\partial w_{ij})^2 \ge 0$, with equality iff every $\alpha_{ij} (\partial E\{r\mid W\}/\partial w_{ij})^2 = 0$, hence iff $\nabla_W E\{r \mid W\} = 0$ when all $\alpha_{ij} > 0$.

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 3 to expand inner product
nodes.statement: Substitute $E\{\Delta w_{ij} \mid W\} = \alpha_{ij} \partial E\{r \mid W\}/\partial w_{ij}$ from Lemma 3 into $\sum_{(i,j)} E\{\Delta w_{ij} \mid W\} \partial E\{r \mid W\}/\partial w_{ij}$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Result equals $\sum_{(i,j)\in I} \alpha_{ij}(\partial E\{r \mid W\}/\partial w_{ij})^2 \ge 0$, with equality conditions following identically to Theorem 1.

nodes.name: Identity from differentiating normalization
nodes.statement: From $\sum_y g = 1$, $\sum_y g \, \partial \ln g / \partial \mu = \partial(\sum_y g)/\partial \mu = 0$ (equation (15)).

nodes.name: Identity from differentiating mean constraint
nodes.statement: From $\mu = \sum_y y g$, $\sum_y (y - \mu) g \, \partial \ln g/\partial \mu = \partial \mu/\partial \mu = 1$ (equation (16)).

nodes.name: Substitute exponential-family form
nodes.statement: By the hypothesis, $\partial \ln g / \partial \mu = \alpha y + \beta$ with $\alpha = \partial Q / \partial \mu$, $\beta = \partial D/\partial \mu$. Compute $\sum_y g (\alpha y + \beta) = \alpha \mu + \beta$ and $\sum_y (y - \mu) g (\alpha y + \beta) = \alpha \sigma^2$.

nodes.name: Solve for alpha, beta and conclude
nodes.statement: Combining (15) with (17) gives $\alpha \mu + \beta = 0$; combining (16) with (18) gives $\alpha \sigma^2 = 1$. Hence $\alpha = 1/\sigma^2$, $\beta = -\mu/\sigma^2$, so $\partial \ln g/\partial \mu = (y - \mu)/\sigma^2$.

nodes.name: Bernoulli unit equivalent to two-action stochastic automaton
nodes.statement: A Bernoulli unit with no input adapting parameter $p_i$ is equivalent to a two-action stochastic learning automaton with actions $\{0,1\}$ and characteristic eligibility $\partial \ln g_i/\partial p_i = (y_i - p_i)/[p_i(1-p_i)]$.

nodes.name: AR-I as REINFORCE on Bernoulli-logistic networks
nodes.statement: Setting $\lambda = 0$ in the AR-P rule recovers $\Delta w_{ij} = \alpha r(y_i - p_i) x_j$, which equals the REINFORCE update (8); hence AR-I on Bernoulli-logistic networks is a REINFORCE algorithm.

nodes.name: Gaussian unit search behavior
nodes.statement: For a Gaussian unit optimizing a function of one real variable, REINFORCE with reinforcement comparison narrows or broadens the search around $\mu$ depending on whether better/worse-than-recent values are sampled within or outside $\sigma$ of the mean.

nodes.name: Bias-only Bernoulli unit with $b = 0$ vs reinforcement comparison
nodes.statement: A single bias-only Bernoulli-logistic unit with $b = 0$ and always-positive $r$ exhibits a biased random walk that may converge to the inferior output, whereas reinforcement comparison with $b$ between the two reinforcement values produces motion always toward the better output.

nodes.name: Non-model-based character of REINFORCE
nodes.statement: REINFORCE algorithms climb the gradient of expected reinforcement without explicitly computing or storing a gradient estimate; this distinguishes them from model-based reinforcement learners.

nodes.name: Convergence properties limitation
nodes.statement: The analysis does not predict asymptotic behavior of REINFORCE; convergence is not guaranteed, and even when it occurs there is typically a nonzero probability of converging to inferior fixed points (illustrated by 2-action LR-I).

nodes.name: Variance-minimizing baseline
nodes.statement: The baseline that minimizes the variance of individual weight changes (Williams 1986; Dayan 1990) is not the mean reinforcement but a more difficult-to-estimate quantity; empirically it gives only a slight improvement over reinforcement comparison.

nodes.name: Eligibility-form variants
nodes.statement: Replacing the factor $y - p$ with $y - \bar{y}$ (an exponentially averaged output) in REINFORCE generally yields faster, more reliable convergence empirically, though without a complete analytical justification.

nodes.name: Stationarity and independence of inputs and reinforcements
nodes.statement: Throughout, the environment's choice of input is independent across time and drawn from a stationary distribution, and the environment's reinforcement value for a given input/output pair is drawn from a stationary distribution; these make $E\{r \mid W\}$ a well-defined deterministic function of $W$.
